cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is writing a letter to the church in Corinth. He just asked them whether they want him to come with a rod, or in love and with a gentle spirit (1 Corinthians 4:21). Now he turns to a report about them: there's sexual immorality among them, and a man has his father's wife.

cards.question: Paul says this kind of sexual immorality isn't tolerated even among ___.
A man in the Corinthian church has his father's wife. How does Paul say the Corinthians are acting about it?

cards.text: Paul says they should have been stricken with grief instead. That's like the smoke alarm SCREAMING and everybody in the kitchen standing around bragging about how good the place smells.

cards.question: Paul says the church should have removed the man who has his father's wife from their ___.

cards.text: Paul isn't in Corinth. He's absent from them in body, but he says he's present with them in spirit.

cards.question: Paul says he'll wait until he gets to Corinth to pronounce judgment on the man who has his father's wife.

cards.text: When they're assembled in the name of the Lord Jesus, with Paul there in spirit and the power of the Lord Jesus, they're to hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh. That's heavy, friend, but Paul gives a reason.

cards.question: Paul says the man is handed over to Satan for a reason. What does Paul want for the man's spirit on the Day of the Lord?

cards.text: Paul tells them their boasting is not good. Then he pulls an example straight out of the KITCHEN, and friend, I just hopped so high my gold base left the ground.

cards.question: Paul says a little leaven works through the whole batch of dough.

cards.text: So Paul says to get rid of the old leaven, so they can be a new unleavened batch, as they really are. Out it goes, like the dough I kept saying I'd use "tomorrow" for THREE weeks.

cards.question: Paul says Christ has been sacrificed. Which feast's lamb does Paul call Christ?

cards.text: So Paul says let's keep the feast. But not with the old bread, leavened with malice and wickedness.

cards.question: Instead of old bread leavened with malice and wickedness, Paul says to keep the feast with the ___ bread of sincerity and of truth.

cards.text: Next, Paul brings up an earlier letter where he told the Corinthians not to associate with sexually immoral people. Now he spells out what he meant.

cards.question: Paul meant the Corinthians should stay away from every sexually immoral person in the world.

cards.text: Paul says he wasn't including the sexually immoral, the greedy, swindlers or idolaters of this world, or they'd have to leave this world. Friend, it took an ANGEL to get me out of one junk drawer.

cards.question: Paul's earlier letter said not to associate with sexually immoral people. Who does Paul now say he means?

answers.text: Anyone who claims to be a brother but is immoral or greedy
Anyone outside the church who is immoral or greedy
Anyone in Corinth who has never heard of Jesus

cards.text: Paul names what he means: someone who's sexually immoral or greedy, an idolater or a verbal abuser, a drunkard or a swindler.

cards.question: Paul says that with someone who claims to be a brother but is sexually immoral or greedy, an idolater or a verbal abuser, a drunkard or a swindler, do not even ___ with him.

cards.text: Then Paul asks what business it is of his to judge those outside the church, and whether the Corinthians aren't to judge those inside.

cards.question: Paul says God will judge those outside the church.
Paul ends with a command for the church about the wicked man. What is it?

answers.text: Pray for him day and night
Send him to Paul at once

findings.problem: The card says Paul, the apostle, is writing a letter to the church in Corinth. This fact comes from outside the passage, since 1 Corinthians 5:1 doesn't name the writer or the recipients. The card gives no reference for it, such as 1 Corinthians 1:1-2. The 4:21 context line has a reference, but the authorship line does not.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "For it to be judged" is one a baker could argue for. The passage is about judging this man: Paul has already pronounced judgment on him in 5:3, and the Day of the Lord is easy to read as a day of judgment. That makes it a near-match, not a clearly false option.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Story card 12 already tells the baker to be "a new unleavened batch," which gives away "unleavened" before card 15 asks for it. The question also says "Instead of old bread leavened with...", which rules out the wrong answer "leavened" in the setup. That leaves only a two-way choice.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Most of the story cards in stop 2 (cards 1, 5 and 7) are flat retellings with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Card 3 is the only one with any personality. Moments like the rhetorical "What business of mine is it to judge those outside?" could hold a real laugh without muddying a fact. The same flatness shows in stop 1, cards 6 and 14.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
